title: In Space, Metal Just Sticks to Metal
hook: Two clean pieces of metal that touch in a vacuum can bond as if welded
summary: In a vacuum, clean surfaces of the same metal can bond on contact without any heat. Spacecraft designers have to watch out for it.

text: Galileo, the probe sent to Jupiter.

In air, metal surfaces are coated with thin oxide layers and grease.
That's why they don't stick when they touch.
